text: When a fetus dies after day 35 (once bones have formed), it cannot be reabsorbed and instead mummifies — sunken eyes, dried dark-brown appearance, intact bones — and is delivered alongside the rest of the litter. Distinguishing by pattern: Parvovirus produces many mummified piglets of varying small sizes (30–160 mm). Aujeszky disease produces mummified piglets alongside weak live piglets, some showing convulsions. PRRS typically produces just 2–3 mummified piglets per litter, often with delivery 3–4 days early. CSF causes fetal death through gestation, producing both weak and mummified piglets, with a distinctive sign being some live newborns trembling.
